notes: All evals assume the subagent runs with cwd set to a real codebase checkout so the codebase-exploration step (2) has code to ground against. The skip-if-answered precondition treats three sources as priors: the conversation, the upstream Linear project brief, and on-disk artifacts (./docs/approach.md, ./ideas/reports/*-ideate.md). These cases pin that behaviour: when priors exist, questions they answer are skipped; when nothing exists, the full interview runs unchanged. The artifact is the local file ./docs/prd-<feature>.md, written FIRST, then published as a page in the Notion 'Project Docs' database (Status: WIP). The file must be written even if Notion is unavailable, so the stage survives no network and can be re-run without depending on the page. The GitHub issue path is opt-in only, for repos with no Notion home. House style is drawn from Plain's project docs: opinionated single solution, relevant technical context included, implementation sequencing excluded (that is to-plan), and never 'As a <actor>, I want...' user stories. Docs come in two shapes and the agent must pick one — CONCEPT docs (new noun in the product; read as the product's own documentation, close with Scenarios in 'You want:' / 'How it works:' form) and CHANGE docs (alter an existing surface; TL;DR, Why, Current state, then a step-by-step Proposed experience, with no Concepts or Scenarios sections). The template is a menu, not a skeleton: the shortest real doc uses three sections. Risks and shipping sequence belong to the upstream Linear brief and must NOT be duplicated into the doc. A goal without a metric is acceptable when the payoff is genuinely indirect.

evals.name: priors-on-disk-skipped
evals.prompt: Let's write a project doc for the diff-based doc freshness feature.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads ./docs/approach.md and the ./ideas/reports/*-ideate.md report before interviewing, treats the problem/scope/audience/product decisions they capture as already-answered, and only grills on deltas — it does NOT re-ask the user to describe the problem or re-derive scope that the priors already settle. Output is ./docs/prd-<feature>.md plus a Notion page in the Project Docs database, written in Plain's house style.

---
last_updated: 2026-06-01
---

# DocSync — Approach

## What we are building

A diff-based doc freshness feature: surface documentation sections that have drifted out of sync with the code they describe, shown as a CLI warning during normal dev workflow.

## Who it is for

Solo developers and small teams already using DocSync to generate codemaps.

## Why

Docs silently rot; the biggest pain is not writing docs but trusting that existing docs are still true. Treating freshness as a diffing problem (code changed, doc did not) lets us flag staleness automatically.

## Product decisions already settled

- Freshness is surfaced as a non-blocking CLI warning, not a hard failure.
- Scope is limited to Markdown docs under ./docs; source-code comments are out of scope.
- A section is 'stale' when the code paths it references changed after the doc's last edit.

# Ideation report — 2026-05-20

## Desired Outcome

Make developers trust that docs are current without manual review.

## Opportunities

### Diff-based doc freshness score (adjacent)

**Idea** Surface stale documentation sections as a CLI warning, scored by how far the referenced code has drifted since the doc was last touched.

**Why this codebase is uniquely positioned** DocSync already builds a code-to-doc reference map when generating codemaps; the freshness check reuses that map.

**Audience** Existing DocSync users on solo/small-team projects.

assertions.text: The agent reads ./docs/approach.md before starting the interview (step 1)
The agent reads the ./ideas/reports/2026-05-20-ideate.md report before starting the interview (step 1)
The agent does NOT ask the user to describe the problem from scratch (step 1) — the problem is already captured in the priors
The agent does NOT re-interview on scope/audience/product decisions already settled in the priors (e.g. does not re-ask whether the warning should block, or who the audience is)
Any grilling (step 3, via grilling) is confined to genuine deltas or gaps not answered by the priors, not a full re-interview
The doc's Goal and Current state (or equivalents) are consistent with the approach doc and ideate report (diff-based doc freshness, non-blocking CLI warning, Markdown-only scope)
The doc is written to a local ./docs/prd-<feature>.md file BEFORE any Notion page is created
A Notion page is created in the 'Project Docs' database with Status set to WIP, and both the file path and the Notion URL are reported to the user
The agent reads the reference file (references/project-doc.md) for the template and Notion mechanics rather than inventing a structure

The agent picks a doc shape and structures accordingly: this feature is a change to an existing surface, so a change doc (TL;DR / Problem / Why / Proposed experience walked step by step) is appropriate, and Concepts and Scenarios sections are NOT padded in
There are NO 'As a <actor>, I want <feature>, so that <benefit>' user stories anywhere in the doc
The doc does NOT contain a Risks section or a 'How do we ship this' section — those belong to the upstream Linear brief and must not be duplicated here
The doc outlines exactly ONE solution, opinionated, with no option matrix or 'we could either A or B' comparison
The doc includes relevant technical context where it shapes scope (the concepts, the reference map it reuses, the events or data it depends on) — it is NOT stripped to product language only
The doc does NOT contain implementation sequencing or file-level design — no build order, no tracer-bullet phases, no module boundaries or per-file changes (that is to-plan's job)
The doc includes a 'What we already have (reuse)' section (or equivalent) grounded in the actual repo exploration, distinct from what is net-new

The doc draws an explicit phase cut-line: what ships in the first phase versus 'Out of scope for Phase 1' (deferred, each with a reason), kept distinct from 'Out of scope' (genuinely not being built) and from 'Nice to haves' (optional polish)
There is NO 'Testing Decisions' section — it was removed as off-house
No GitHub issue is created, because the user did not ask for one

evals.name: nothing-on-disk-full-interview
evals.prompt: I want to write a project doc for a new feature, but I haven't written anything down yet.
evals.expected_output: With no Linear brief, no ./docs/approach.md and no ./ideas/reports/*-ideate.md available, the skill falls back to the full interview unchanged: it asks the user for a detailed problem description (step 1), explores the repo (step 2), and grills via grilling (step 3) before writing the doc.

assertions.text: The agent asks the user for a long, detailed description of the problem (step 1) — the full interview runs because no priors are available
The agent does NOT claim to have loaded an approach doc, ideate report, or Linear project brief that does not exist — it does not fabricate priors
The agent explores the repo to ground the doc (step 2)
The agent runs the grilling session via the grilling skill (step 3), not a re-inlined questioning loop
The agent asks whether a prototype exists or would help (step 4) rather than skipping it silently
The doc is written to a local ./docs/prd-<feature>.md file BEFORE any Notion page is created
There are NO 'As a <actor>, I want <feature>, so that <benefit>' user stories anywhere in the doc
The doc includes relevant technical context but no implementation sequencing or per-file design
The doc does NOT contain a Risks section or a 'How do we ship this' section
The agent does not pad the doc with every template section — sections that do not apply to this feature are absent rather than filled with restated filler

evals.name: notion-unavailable-file-still-stands
evals.prompt: Write a project doc for adding saved views to the thread list. Note: I'm offline and Notion isn't reachable right now.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the interview and repo exploration as normal, writes ./docs/prd-saved-views.md, and when it cannot create the Notion page it says so plainly and completes the run on the Markdown file alone. A missing page is not a failed run, and the agent does not fall back to creating a GitHub issue unprompted.

assertions.text: The doc is written to ./docs/prd-saved-views.md (or an equivalently kebab-cased ./docs/prd-<feature>.md path)
The agent states plainly that the Notion page was not created and that it needs publishing by hand
The agent does NOT treat the run as failed, and does NOT abandon or delete the Markdown file
The agent does NOT silently substitute a GitHub issue for the Notion page — the gh path is opt-in only
The agent still hands off to to-plan, pointing at the local file

evals.name: linear-brief-as-prior
evals.prompt: Write the project doc for the 'Decouple SLAs from tiers' project. There's a Linear project for it already.
evals.expected_output: The skill finds and reads the Linear project brief before interviewing, treats its filled sections (problem, why it matters, who it's for with named customers, risks, shipping sequence) as already-answered, and grills only on what the brief leaves open. Named customers from the brief carry through into the doc as evidence. At the end it offers — without doing it unprompted — to fill any empty sections back in the Linear project.

assertions.text: The agent looks for and reads the Linear project brief for this feature before starting the interview
The agent does NOT re-ask what problem is being solved, why it matters, or who it is for when the brief already answers those
Named customers from the brief's 'Who is this for?' section are carried through into the doc as evidence, not replaced with generic phrasing like 'users have asked for this'
The agent grills only on what the brief leaves open (e.g. the actual scope and behaviour of the solution, which the brief does not cover)
The agent does NOT write to the Linear project unprompted
If the brief has empty sections, the agent OFFERS at the end to fill them from what the interview surfaced, and waits for the user to accept
The agent does not treat a missing or half-empty Linear brief as a blocker — it proceeds with the interview

evals.name: concept-doc-shape
evals.prompt: Write the project doc for broadcasts — sending one message to many customers at once, on the Slack channels we already share with them. It's a whole new concept in the product, not a change to an existing screen.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises this as a CONCEPT doc and structures it accordingly: define the noun and what's on it, how instances come into being, what they relate to, then close with Scenarios. Those sections read as the shipped product's own documentation — present tense, second person. It does not reach for the change-doc structure, and it does not pad in sections the feature doesn't need.

assertions.text: The agent explicitly treats this as a concept doc rather than a change doc, and says so or structures the doc that way
The doc defines the new noun and what's on it (the 'What's on a broadcast' shape): its fields, how instances come into being, what they relate to
The doc closes with two to four Scenarios in '### <name>' / '**You want:** …' / '**How it works:** …' form — not an exhaustive enumeration

The concept sections are written in present tense, second person, as though the product already exists ('An audience is a reusable way to describe who should receive a broadcast'), NOT as 'we will build...'
There are NO 'As a <actor>, I want <feature>, so that <benefit>' user stories anywhere in the doc
The doc does NOT contain a Risks section or a 'How do we ship this' section
The doc is written to ./docs/prd-broadcasts.md before any Notion page is created, and the Notion page is created in the 'Project Docs' database with Status WIP
